topIssues.title: latest-op-sepolia-reth-archive/ returns 403 while other latest-* symlinks work correctly
topIssues.author: toshihiko-okubo
topIssues.body:
<!--
Need help?
Refer to our contributing guidelines for additional information about making a good issue:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Bug Description**
`https://datadirs.optimism.io/latest-op-sepolia-reth-archive/` returns HTTP 403,
while other `latest-*` paths (e.g. `latest-mainnet-reth-full/`) correctly redirect
to the latest snapshot. The symlink appears to be stale — last modified April 6, 2026 —
while actual snapshot files from May 2026 exist at the root.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Send a request to `https://datadirs.optimism.io/latest-op-sepolia-reth-archive/`
2. Observe HTTP 403 response

**Expected behavior**
`https://datadirs.optimism.io/latest-op-sepolia-reth-archive/` should redirect to
the latest available op-sepolia reth archive snapshot, as `latest-mainnet-reth-full/`
does for mainnet.

As of writing, the expected redirect target would be:
`https://datadirs.optimism.io/mainnet-op-sepolia-reth-archive-2026-05-25.tar.zst`

**Environment Information:**
 - Operating System: N/A (server-side issue on datadirs.optimism.io)
 - Package Version: N/A

**Configurations:**
N/A

**Logs:**
```bash
curl -I https://datadirs.optimism.io/latest-op-sepolia-reth-archive/
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Server: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu)
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 02:13:38 GMT
Content-Type: text/html
Content-Length: 162
Connection: keep-alive
```

**Additional context**
This may be related to the unchecked item in ethereum-optimism/infra#536:
> `- [ ] Fix naming and symlink inconsistencies`

topPRs.title: feat(op-conductor-ops): migrate to apko + melange
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Migrate `op-conductor-ops` from a hand-written `python:3.12-slim-bookworm` Dockerfile to a declarative apko + melange build using upstream Wolfi packages and the factory `apko.yaml` reusable workflow.

The Dockerfile was previously running \`poetry install\` inside the container at **runtime** (every container start), and the launcher script ran a fresh \`poetry install\` again. With apko, every dependency is resolved at build time as a signed Wolfi apk, the wheel is built via PEP 517 (\`python -m build\` → installer), and the main container has no shell, no poetry, and no pip.

## Project changes

- Move flat-file Python modules into a proper \`op_conductor_ops/\` package directory; convert sibling imports (\`from network import …\`) to relative (\`from .network import …\`).
- Wrap the typer entrypoint in a \`main()\` function so it can be registered as a \`[tool.poetry.scripts]\` entry.
- Update \`pyproject.toml\`:
    - Drop \`package-mode = false\`.
    - Add \`version = "0.0.1"\` and \`packages = [{ include = "op_conductor_ops" }]\`.
    - Register the \`op-conductor-ops\` console script at \`op_conductor_ops.cli:main\`.
- Drop the legacy shell launcher that ran \`poetry install\` at container startup. apko-built images install everything at build time.

## Build changes

- Add \`op-conductor-ops/melange.yaml\`. One pipeline step: \`uses: python/build-wheel\`. The PEP 517 frontend reads \`pyproject.toml\` and invokes \`poetry-core\` to produce a wheel. The runtime closure is declared via Wolfi apk names mirroring \`[tool.poetry.dependencies]\`.
- Add \`op-conductor-ops/apko/op-conductor-ops.apko.yaml\`. Pulls \`wolfi-baselayout\`, \`ca-certificates-bundle\`, \`tzdata\`, and the melange-produced \`op-conductor-ops\` apk. Runs as uid 65532 (non-root).
- Update \`.github/images.json\`: add \`op-conductor-ops\` as a \`groups\` entry (\`mode: apko\`, \`services: [op-conductor-ops]\`) and remove it from the Dockerfile-mode \`images\` map.
- Update \`branches.yaml\` + \`tags.yaml\`: replace the legacy \`detect-changes\` / \`parse-tag\` actions with \`factory/actions/plan\` and add a job that calls \`factory/.github/workflows/apko.yaml\` for the \`op-conductor-ops\` group.

## Verified locally

\`\`\`
$ docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 op-conductor-ops:apko-test-amd64 --help
 Usage: op-conductor-ops [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
 CLI for managing OP Conductor sequencers.
   ...
\`\`\`

Image rebuilt cleanly with no manual fiddling. melange's SCA emitted the runtime closure auto-detected from the wheel's METADATA file (no manual \`pip install\` step needed).

## Test plan

- [ ] Branch CI: factory \`plan\` action emits \`op-conductor-ops\` under \`groups_matrix_json\`; \`apko.yaml\` reusable workflow runs and publishes \`us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-conductor-ops:<branch>\`
- [ ] Smoke test passes: \`op-conductor-ops --version\` returns successfully
- [ ] Tag push (\`op-conductor-ops/v<semver>\`) builds and publishes the same image at the version tag
- [ ] Existing Dockerfile-mode images (cci-stats, op-acceptor, etc.) keep building unchanged via the \`local\` matrix job

## Pattern

This PR is the first apko migration in this repo. The \`groups\` shape in \`.github/images.json\` plus the dedicated job in \`branches.yaml\` is intended to be reused for subsequent migrations — one group entry + one job per migrated image (or one group with multiple services if they share a melange config).

topPRs.title: feat(op-conductor-ops): add bootstrap-standby-cluster command
topPRs.author: zhwrd
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds a new `bootstrap-standby-cluster` command to `op-conductor-ops`.
- Forms a fresh raft cluster across the configured conductor/sequencer pairs but leaves every conductor paused and does not start a sequencer.
- Intended for standing up a new set of nodes that will follow an existing network as verifiers, ready to take over sequencing later via `resume` and `force-active-sequencer`.

## Behavior

Compared with the existing `bootstrap-cluster`, the new command:

- Still waits for all conductor/sequencer RPCs to be reachable.
- Adds stricter preconditions: aborts if any sequencer is active **or** any conductor is unpaused.
- Still locates the bootstrapped raft leader and runs `update_cluster_membership` to populate voters/non-voters.
- **Skips** `force_active_sequencer`, the `is_healthy` wait, and the final `resume`.

The `--sequencer-start-timeout` option (env `BOOTSTRAP_SEQUENCER_START_TIMEOUT`) is shared with `bootstrap-cluster`; no new envvar is introduced.

## Test plan

This CLI has no automated test suite. Manual verification on a devnet is pending:

- [ ] On a devnet with all conductors paused and one started with `raftBootstrap=true`, run `op-conductor-ops bootstrap-standby-cluster <network>` and confirm exit 0 plus the success message.
- [ ] Run `op-conductor-ops status <network>` and confirm `conductor_active == False` and `sequencer_active == False` for every node, with correct voter/non-voter membership.
- [ ] Run `op-conductor-ops resume <network>` and `op-conductor-ops force-active-sequencer <network> <leader-id>` and confirm normal sequencing kicks in (the standby state is a valid starting point for the existing flow).
- [ ] Exercise the precondition guards: an active sequencer, an unpaused conductor, and a network with no bootstrapped leader should each abort with a clear, actionable error.

topPRs.title: [codex] fix proxyd interop access-list namespace
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Updates proxyd interop access-list validation to call `interop_checkAccessList` directly instead of using the pinned op-geth helper that still calls `supervisor_checkAccessList`.

## Why

`ethereum-optimism/optimism#20778` moved op-interop-filter's query API to the `interop` RPC namespace. Proxyd still depended on op-geth's `InteropClient`, whose `CheckAccessList` method sends the old `supervisor_checkAccessList` method.

I checked the available client libraries before making this local wrapper change: the current OP `op-service/sources.SupervisorClient` and the pinned op-geth helper both still use the legacy namespace, so a small proxyd-side RPC call is the narrowest fix.

## Validation

- `go test . -run TestPerformCheckAccessListOpUsesInteropNamespace -count=1`
- `go test ./integration_tests -run TestInteropValidation_NormalFlow -count=1 -timeout=90s`

Note: `go test ./...` reached the existing `proxyd/integration_tests` 10m timeout in a broader run; the focused interop validation flow passes when run directly.
